title: fix(pm): claim-branch-unparsed remedy names the whole shape its own rule requires
body:
Fixes #19414

Clause-②: no

## What moved

Only the `claim-branch-unparsed` remedy sentence in `claimBranchUnparsedGap`, the one docblock line that restates it, and ONE self-test case. The reader is untouched: `CLAIM_SELECTION_RULE`, row C8 and the retraction channel read exactly as they did at `57ceb9d`. Net +21 lines in `scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs` (26 insertions / 5 deletions), against the dispatch's ceiling of +30.

Placeholder note: the literal in the source spells its two placeholders in angle-bracket form. They are written as `N` and `slug` everywhere in this body, because the body sanitizer eats short angle-bracket fragments, fenced or not.

### Before — `57ceb9d`, the sentence at :4913–:4915

> Remedy — the CLAIMING SEAT, with one comment: name the branch on a `Branch:` line of its OWN (`` Branch: `claude/issue-N-slug` ``), ⛔ not inside the `Claim:` sentence, which no reader parses.

The rule sentence printed in the SAME output (`pair.1.claim.rule`) requires both lines:

> the GOVERNING claim — the NEWEST comment whose body carries a line beginning `Claim:`/`Claimed:` … AND whose `Branch:` line parses at least one protocol-shaped branch

A `Branch:` line alone carries no claim marker, so the comment the old sentence prescribed is not a claim comment at all: `claimGovernance` never sees it, `newest` stays the unparsed claim, and the state does not move.

### After

> Remedy — the CLAIMING SEAT, with ONE comment carrying BOTH lines: a line beginning `Claim:` AND a `Branch:` line of its OWN (`` Branch: `claude/issue-N-slug` ``). ⛔ Not the branch named inside the `Claim:` sentence, which no reader parses, and ⛔ not a `Branch:` line posted ALONE in a comment of its own, which carries no claim marker and is therefore not a claim comment at all — that comment leaves this state exactly as it is. ⚠️ Already holding a LIVE claim on this card? Post `Release:` FIRST, so the new comment is the only claim standing — a second `Claim:` under a live one is row C8, ⛔ not a repair.

The old warning is kept verbatim in substance — the defect is what the sentence OMITTED, not what it said — and the phrase the existing self-test pins (`` `Branch:` line of its OWN ``) is unmoved.

## The filer's four steps, reproduced on this tree

Offline through `--pair-json` (fixtures only, no board read), each exit captured before any pipe:

| step | the card thread | exit |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | one live claim naming its branch INSIDE the `Claim:` sentence | **2** — `claim-branch-unparsed` |
| 2 | …the OLD remedy followed: a `Branch:` line of its own, in a comment of its own | **2** — unchanged, the remedy did nothing |
| 3 | …`Claim:` + `Branch:` added under the still-live claim | **4** — row C8 |
| 4 | …`Release:` then ONE fresh claim | **0** |

That is the filer's measured path (2 → 2 → 4 → 0), reproduced before the edit and unchanged after it: the sentence moved, the reader did not.

Following the sentence as it NOW reads, from the same step-1 thread — `Release:` first, then ONE comment carrying both lines — reaches **exit 0 in one act** (2 → 0).

## The self-test case is the sentence's own proof

Four assertions, beside the existing `#17149` battery:

1. a `Branch:` line posted ALONE leaves the thread at `claim-branch-unparsed` — the old remedy's own outcome, pinned;
2. the comment the sentence now prescribes (both lines, the live claim released first) IS the governing claim — `cardDeclaration(...).state === 'declared'` and zero finding rows;
3. CONTROL: post that same comment WITHOUT the `Release:` and row C8 answers — which is why the sentence names it;
4. the printed sentence carries the whole shape: `ONE comment carrying BOTH lines`, `` `Release:` FIRST `` and `row C8`.

`node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --self-test` → **exit 0**, 1075 cases pass (was 1071).

### Reverse verification — the sentence assertion really can fail

Through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor must hit; the write is verified against the disk, and the restore against `HEAD`), from the committed state:

```
ablation-replace:   replaced 1 occurrence(s)
ablation-replace: ok mutation landed: anchor 1 -> 0, blob de6a171ba88a -> efcc146d09eb
  ✗ …and the sentence itself carries the whole shape: both lines, the `Release:` before a second claim, and the row one earns
✗ check-clause2-carriers self-test: 1 of 1075 case(s) failed.
ablation-replace: ok restored: blob == HEAD (de6a171ba88a) and `git diff HEAD` is empty
```

Assertions 1–3 pin the READER, which this diff does not touch; assertion 3 is their non-vacuity control (same thread, one thing changed, C8 instead of silence).
